records.stepTherapy: Generic fluticasone propionate HFA carries the Restricted Access/Step Therapy flag on this plan; step criteria are on the plan's prior-review page (PDF p.3, printed II), not in this document.
records.verificationNote: PDF p.38 (printed p.30): budesonide inhalation suspension (generic, nebulizer) Tier 1 with no flags, chosen as the only no-restriction Tier 1 ICS. Fluticasone HFA 44 mcg is Tier 1 but carries RA/ST and QL flags, so it is listed as a step barrier. Judgment call: fluticasone HFA is more commonly prescribed in practice, but the brief rule (cheapest tier, no PA/step) selects budesonide nebulizer. Flovent brand not listed. Document is not a closed list, so no ICS is inferred as nonformulary. [Sonnet check 2026-10-21: Pick changed from budesonide nebulizer to Qvar Redihaler. Qvar is a handheld inhaler with no PA/step flag (Tier 2, QL only; PDF p.38), so a prescriber can write it without the step that generic fluticasone HFA 44 (Tier 1, RA/ST + QL; 110/220 is Tier 3, RA + QL) needs. Budesonide nebulizer (Tier 1, no flags) stays as the cheapest option but is a nebulizer, not what an adult asthma/COPD inhaler guide would lead with. Arnuity Ellipta (Tier 2, QL; PDF p.37) added. Flovent not listed; no ICS inferred as nonformulary.]

records.verificationNote: Read directly from the UnitedHealthcare 2026 Prescription Drug List (PDL), effective January 1, 2026, page 48 (Respiratory Tract / Pulmonary Agents - Drugs for Asthma and COPD section), and page 5 (Symbols key: E = may be excluded from coverage or subject to PA in CT, NJ, NY; PA = prior authorization required; QL = quantity limit). Confirmed: 'albuterol sulfate hfa aerosol solution 108 (90 base) mcg/act inhalation' is listed as Tier 2 with QL. PROVENTIL HFA and VENTOLIN HFA (brand equivalents) are both marked 'E' indicating PA/exclusion eligibility rather than clean coverage. Levalbuterol hcl inhalation and LEVALBUTEROL HFA/XOPENEX HFA are Tier 3 with QL (covered but non-preferred, higher cost-share). Nebulizer solution and oral syrup forms of generic albuterol sulfate are confirmed Tier 1. Sig/dosing (2 puffs q4-6h PRN) is standard SABA rescue dosing per FDA label, not stated verbatim in the PDL (the PDL lists coverage/tier only, not directions for use) -- inferred from standard clinical practice, hence marking sig details as inferred within an overall verified coverage picture. [Reused: same national UHC commercial PDL as the MD guide (2026-10-21); outside CT/NJ/NY its 'E' symbol means may be excluded]
